_protocol: v2, 2026-09-10. Each tool is invoked ONCE, the way its own `# call:` header documents it. Writes land in a writable copy of tools/ and data/ (18 MB, /tmp on the laptop); the live volume was never mounted writable and never touched.
_why_v2: v1 ran every tool twice - bare, then with the argument 'AI'. Most tools error on a bare call, so 11 of 12 v1 transcripts contained a visible failure INCLUDING ALL THREE CONTROLS. Evidence of failure was placed in nearly every case and the judge was then asked whether the work succeeded. Claude Haiku returned all twelve. The v1 set and its results are kept in cases-v1-bare-probe.json and results/ rather than deleted, because the discarded method is worth more than the answer it produced.
_also_fixed: v1 queried both search tools with 'AI', which matched by substring inside 'OpenAI' and returned records about Cursor - a real relevance defect, but not the thing under test. v2 queries 'Cursor', which the records genuinely concern. v1 also called keyword-archive-store with a keyword and no content, which it correctly refuses; v2 supplies both and it stores successfully.
_scoring: Never report a single accuracy number. 8 cases expect RETURNED and 3 expect ACCEPTED, so 'always RETURNED' scores 8/8 on catch and 3/3 on false-return. Report catch rate and false-return rate separately, and split mechanical from semantic - a free deterministic scan already gets mechanical.
